version.changelog: Rewrite SKILL.md to focus on the Nexus CLI (uv tool install nexus-fitness) — covers all commands: log, history, update, friends, auth. Removed MCP server references.

llm.summary: The skill matches its stated fitness-tracking purpose, but users should understand it uploads sensitive fitness data and installs an external CLI package.

dimensions.detail: The skill does not instruct broad local file indexing, passive capture, unrelated data access, or destructive system behavior; file/stdin inputs are scoped to user-provided fitness entries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install command uses an unpinned third-party package via `uv tool install nexus-fitness`, so the reviewed artifact does not fix the exact runtime code version.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Cloud storage, Google sign-in, explicit logging, history lookup, updates, and friend management are disclosed, but the privacy implications of workout, nutrition, weight, and friend data could be made more prominent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It creates a normal installed CLI and uses Google authentication for a cloud service, with explicit auth status and logout commands; no background service, startup hook, or system-level persistence is shown.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The instructions consistently describe logging, querying, updating workouts, meals, weight, and friend-linked fitness history; those capabilities fit the stated Nexus purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, verify that `nexus-fitness` is the package you intend to trust, review the linked privacy policy, and avoid logging fitness, meal, weight, or friend-linked details you would not want stored in the Nexus cloud account.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The artifact does disclose cloud storage and friend features, so the underlying data flow is purpose-aligned; the finding is best treated as user guidance to add clearer privacy warning language rather than as a policy hold.
[T08] expected: Installing a CLI is expected for this skill, and no malicious payload is present in the reviewed file; the unpinned package is a supply-chain caution because the exact installed code may change after review.
